findings.title: [P1] Enforce the local transport policy for every HTTP adapter
findings.body: The loader now accepts opted-in HTTP endpoints for every non-CLI provider, but only OpenAIAdapter constructs and passes TransportPolicy. Other HTTP adapters using these helpers retain policy=None, so requests to newly admitted private endpoints can use environment proxies and, on the urllib path, follow redirects. A configured proxy or redirecting local server can consequently receive prompts and credentials intended for the private endpoint. Apply the policy centrally or require every adapter to pass it before admitting insecure endpoints for that provider type.
findings.description: The loader now accepts opted-in HTTP endpoints for every non-CLI provider, but only OpenAIAdapter constructs and passes TransportPolicy. A configured proxy or redirecting local server can consequently receive prompts and credentials intended for the private endpoint. findings.failure_mode: The loader now accepts opted-in HTTP endpoints for every non-CLI provider, but only OpenAIAdapter constructs and passes TransportPolicy.

findings.cross_file_justification: endpoint_policy.validate_providers admits an http:// endpoint whenever allow_insecure_endpoint matches the host, with no requirement that the provider be keyless. openai_adapter.complete then attaches `Authorization: Bearer <key>` whenever keyless is false, regardless of scheme, so a real API key travels in cleartext to the opted-in RFC1918/loopback host.
findings.description: The D-7.2 opt-in lets an operator declare `http://10.x.x.x/v1` (or any RFC1918 / loopback host). Nothing at load time or request time ties that opt-in to `keyless: true`. If the provider also has `auth: {env:SOME_KEY}`, the adapter puts the bearer token on a plaintext HTTP request to a LAN host. The health_check path does the same (lines 854-862). The module docstring frames the opt-in as 'nothing is sent in the clear' only for the https-on-local-host case; the http case with a credential is silently allowed.
findings.failure_mode: A vendor API key (or a local server's shared secret) is exposed to any passive observer on the LAN segment or to a compromised intermediate host, and to anyone who can read a packet capture. Prompt content also traverses the LAN in cleartext, but the credential is the durable loss.
findings.suggested_fix: In validate_providers, when `allow_insecure_endpoint` is set and the interpolated endpoint scheme is `http`, require `keyless: true` (or refuse an `auth` value that interpolates a secret). As a belt-and-braces check, have the adapter refuse to add an Authorization header when the request URL scheme is `http` and the provider is not keyless.

findings.cross_file_justification: The load-time gate (endpoint_policy.validate_providers / check_endpoint) admits an http opt-in or a `dispatch_group: local` label for any provider `type`, but the request-time half (TransportPolicy: no proxy env, no redirects, path-prefix) is constructed only in openai_adapter._transport_policy and only passed into http_post/http_get/http_post_stream when the caller supplies `policy=`. Other adapters (e.g. anthropic, bedrock) in providers/ are not touched by this diff and call the transport helpers without a policy.
findings.description: TransportPolicy is opt-in at the call site: `http_post(..., policy=None)` keeps the pre-existing behaviour (urllib default opener follows 3xx and honours proxy env; urllib's redirect handler forwards non-Content-* headers including Authorization). The diff wires the policy only into OpenAIAdapter. A provider of another type that passes the new load-time checks (http to a loopback/RFC1918 host, or https on a local host with `dispatch_group: local`) therefore gets the relaxed endpoint rule without the compensating request-time controls. I could not read the other adapters in this review window, so treat the exploitability as unverified but the gap as structural: the invariant lives in one adapter rather than in the transport layer.
findings.failure_mode: A compromised or malicious local server at the opted-in host answers with a 302 to e.g. http://169.254.169.254/ or an external collector; the urllib fallback follows it and re-sends the request (with Authorization and the prompt) to the redirect target. Proxy environment variables also redirect the 'local' traffic through an arbitrary host.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) restrict `allow_insecure_endpoint` and `dispatch_group: local` at load time to provider types whose adapter is known to apply TransportPolicy (openai/openai_compat today), or better (b) derive the policy inside providers/base.py from ProviderConfig (allow_insecure_endpoint / keyless / local endpoint host) so every adapter gets it without having to remember `policy=`; make the urllib fallback never follow redirects for any request that carries an Authorization header.

findings.description: Any HTTP 400 whose body contains the substrings `response_format` or `json_schema` (any field, any case) makes complete() drop the strict `response_format` and resend the full prompt without schema enforcement (lines 193-205). The decision is driven entirely by the remote server's error text. A server that always 400s on first sight of a schema gets every structured request downgraded to unenforced output, and the prompt is transmitted twice per call. The envelope does record schema_enforced=false / schema_rejected_by_server=true, so telemetry stays truthful, which is why this is LOW rather than higher.
findings.failure_mode: Structured-output guarantees that downstream consumers (verdict/dissent gates) assume for `structured_json` hops can be switched off by the model server, and each affected call is billed twice.
findings.suggested_fix: Tighten the heuristic to the OpenAI error shape (`error.param == 'response_format'` or `error.code` in a known set) rather than substring search over the whole body; cap the downgrade to once per provider per process and surface a visible warning; consider refusing the downgrade when the caller required enforcement (e.g. under a strict budget/verdict gate).

findings.description: complete() applies TransportPolicy when the provider has an opt-in OR the model's dispatch_group is `local` (`_transport_policy`, line ~206). health_check applies it only when `allow_insecure_endpoint` is set. A `dispatch_group: local` provider on an https local host (admitted without opt-in by validate_providers line 315-321) is probed through the legacy path, which honours proxy environment variables and, on the urllib fallback, follows redirects while carrying the Authorization header (when not keyless).
findings.failure_mode: The D-7.2 'no proxy, no redirect' promise is not kept for the health probe of a local https hop; a redirect or proxy env can divert the probe (and credential) off the local host.
findings.suggested_fix: Build the policy in health_check from the same predicate as `_transport_policy` (opt-in OR local endpoint host / any model with dispatch_group local), or compute `TransportPolicy` once on the adapter at construction and reuse it in both paths.

findings.cross_file_justification: endpoint_policy.hop_is_local is documented as the ONE implementation for MODELINV hop_locality (label on entry or provider block, not a CLI hop, endpoint host passes the local-hop rule). modelinv.hop_locality_of instead returns `local` from the model-entry label alone, ignoring the provider-block label, CLI kind and endpoint host.
findings.description: The audit envelope's `hop_locality` is derived from a different rule than the one the loader/planner enforce. Today load-time validation (_local_label_refusal) refuses labels that fail the rule, so the two agree for a config that loaded through load_config; but hop_telemetry receives whatever `hounfour` dict cheval passes, and a provider-block `dispatch_group: local` (allowed by hop_is_local) is reported as `hosted` by this function, while a hand-built or partially-validated dict could report `local` for a hosted host.
findings.failure_mode: MODELINV rows that locality audits rely on (local_voices compliance) can disagree with the planner's decision, under- or over-reporting local hops.
findings.suggested_fix: Have hop_locality_of delegate to endpoint_policy.hop_is_local(hounfour, provider, model_id) (the import guard already allows endpoint_policy imports from modelinv for split_url), so there is a single locality rule.

findings.description: describe_provider is documented as 'never carries a secret value' and is printed to stdout by the CLI for model-health-probe.sh. It emits the post-interpolation `endpoint` verbatim. The auth field is handled via `_raw` to avoid leaking an interpolated value, but the endpoint gets no equivalent treatment, so an endpoint that interpolates `{env:...}` into its path or query (e.g. a gateway key or tenant token in the URL, which the cycle-099 validator only refuses in userinfo) is printed in the clear and may land in probe logs.
findings.failure_mode: A URL-embedded secret appears in CLI output / shell logs captured by the probe script.
findings.suggested_fix: Return only the parts the probe needs (scheme, host, port, path prefix via split_url) or redact any segment that originated from an interpolated secret, mirroring the `_raw` handling for auth.
